clue.text: Inland Revenue acts thus, if about to confront scoundrel

indicators.note: about here signals that the little word if is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a scally is a rogue or scamp, originally Liverpool slang

explanation.surface: The taxman behaves this way if it is about to face down a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confront' is only a link placing the rogue second; the scoundrel word is Liverpool slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax authority acts in financial, fiscal ways, so the adverb describes how Inland Revenue works.

clue.text: DIY units — stuff installed in apartments

indicators.note: installed in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: flats are apartments
to pack is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Self-assembly furniture: things fitted into apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatpacks are furniture kits sold for home self-assembly, so do-it-yourself units.

clue.text: Mark is pulled up about his religion

indicators.note: about here means the reversed letters go around the next word
in a down clue pulled up reads letters from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: Mk is the abbreviation for Mark, the gospel or the old German currency

explanation.surface: Mark is brought up short regarding his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses the abbreviation plus the little word, giving SIKM, and 'about' wraps that round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhism is the monotheistic faith founded in the Punjab by Guru Nanak, so an example of a religion.

clue.text: Female excluded from fair pay review for group of workers?

indicators.note: to review is to rework or revise, so the remaining letters are rearranged
excluded from tells you to take a letter out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Women left out of an equal pay review.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers sounds like employees, but it is bees: worker bees live in hives. Removing F from FAIR PAY leaves AIRPAY, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a collection of beehives, home to colonies of worker bees.

clue.text: Long-term investor who's of help in emergency?

explanation.surface: A long-term saver and a rescuer in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits it as someone who saves for life; the second is the rescuer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer who preserves life; and jokingly, one who saves money across a whole lifetime.

clue.text: Male reporter's area, one close to Paris?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a cub is a novice newspaper reporter

explanation.surface: A man's journalist's beat is close to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the French city, but it is the Trojan prince of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hecuba was queen of Troy and mother of the prince Paris, so a close relative.

clue.text: Striking way of accessing computer system

explanation.surface: Hitting, and breaking into computers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacking can mean hitting or kicking, as in football, and also illicit computer access.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking means kicking or chopping at, and also gaining unauthorised entry to computer networks.

clue.text: Beset by such toil, struggling learner takes it easy

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the scrambled letters go round the learner
struggling suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner sign on cars

explanation.surface: Weighed down by such labour, a failing student relaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges SUCH TOIL; 'Beset by' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill out is informal for to relax, to take things easy.

clue.text: In part of Africa, very much a blessing

indicators.note: in means the intensifier sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
so means very much, as in so tired

explanation.surface: In an African region, a great blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start looks like a preposition setting the scene, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an archaic word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: Put question: answer requires rudiments of scientific knowledge

indicators.note: rudiments are the first basics, so take the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Posing a question whose answer needs basic science.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a question to someone is simply to enquire, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Violation of law, in part

parts.note: a fraction is a part or portion of a whole

explanation.surface: A breach of the law, at least partially.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach or infringement of a rule or law, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Flower power achieved prominence round Pacific area, perhaps

indicators.note: round here means the outer letters surround the inserted piece

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
to rise is to become prominent, past tense rose
the Pacific Rim is the region around that ocean, so rim is an area, given as one example

explanation.surface: A bloom, a force that came to the fore around the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the power-plus-rose letters, PROSE, around the Pacific area.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower, so a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Liberal that is outwardly least fond of Labour?

indicators.note: outwardly means the phrase for that is sits on the outside, around the other piece

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A Liberal who, on the face of it, is the least keen on the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the political party, but it means work; 'outwardly' wraps the Latin phrase round the Liberal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The laziest person is the one least fond of work, with Labour read as toil rather than the party.

clue.text: Prime Minister's bill to bring back party supporters

indicators.note: bringing something back here means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: PM is the standard abbreviation for Prime Minister
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: The PM's account is used to win back the party faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' reverses PM + AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a faction or group of people sharing a cause, so a body of party supporters.

clue.text: One tucks into meringue before noon — it's a sort of reflex

indicators.note: before places the dessert ahead of the noon letter
tucks into means the numeral goes inside the dessert

parts.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Somebody digs into a pavlova before midday by sheer reflex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but it puts I inside PAVLOVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A conditioned reflex is called Pavlovian after the scientist whose dogs salivated at a bell.

clue.text: On the surface, a description of very powdery coffee?

definitions.text: a description of very powdery coffee?

explanation.surface: Above ground, and a way of describing coffee milled too finely.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as over plus ground: coffee ground too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Overground means above the earth, on the surface; humorously it also means ground excessively.

clue.text: Message from. old entertainment centre?

explanation.surface: A message from an old wireless-and-gramophone cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: A radiogram is a radio telegram, and also an old cabinet combining a radio and record player.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a telegram sent by radio and a combined wireless and record player of the mid-century.

clue.text: Daisy pursues man about town

indicators.note: pursues means the flower comes after the other pieces

parts.note: don is a man, as in the Spanish title for a gentleman
C, short for circa, means about
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Daisy chases a man around the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Check out painter entering art school for some illegal business?

indicators.note: entering means the next pieces go inside the art school's name

parts.note: the Slade is the famous art school in London
to vet is to check or examine
RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: Inspecting an artist working at an art college for some shady dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Slade School of Fine Art is part of University College London; RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade in slaves is outlawed commerce, so an example of illegal business.

clue.text: Bishop subsequently taking single mass in …

indicators.note: taking means the outer word holds the following pieces

parts.note: later means subsequently
I is the Roman numeral one, single
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A bishop later said a single Mass in ...
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, which describes what he wore.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer was a Protestant bishop burned at the stake in Oxford in 1555.

clue.text: … suitable apparel? Uncle's thrilled with it

indicators.note: thrilled suggests excitement, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the possessive gives the word uncle

explanation.surface: ... clothes fit for a bishop: the uncle is delighted with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Continuing from 18 down: a tunicle is a garment a bishop wears, so apparel suitable for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunicle is a short liturgical vestment worn by bishops and subdeacons, so fitting dress.

clue.text: Nelson, for example, won battles after a short time

indicators.note: after places the scrambled word behind the time letter

parts.note: T is the short form of time

indicators.note: battles suggests struggling or fighting, so the letters of won are shaken up

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson soon won his battles.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson looks like the admiral, but it is a town in Lancashire (and in New Zealand). 'battles' rearranges WON as OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson is a town in Lancashire, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Rhetorical language unsuitable in this chapel?

explanation.surface: Grand speechmaking would be out of place in this small chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: eloquence is supposedly out of place in a chapel bearing the same name, a place for prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rhetorical speech and a small chapel for private prayer.

clue.text: A second source of water, to boot

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Another water source, in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition, also, besides.

clue.text: Transfer soldiers back to a different service

indicators.note: back tells you to read the soldiers' letters in reverse

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, are soldiers
RN, the Royal Navy, is a service other than the army

explanation.surface: Moving troops back to another branch of the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: In law to attorn is to transfer, as of tenancy or allegiance, to a new owner.

clue.text: Said dessert's also known as a 25 in Athens?

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken that matches the entry in sound

parts.note: mousse is a dessert and aka abbreviates also known as

explanation.surface: Supposedly the pudding has another name as a main dish in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer to 25 across, a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked aubergine and mince dish is a Greek main meal, as typically eaten in Athens.

clue.text: Series of sailing lessons? Some make a meal of it

definitions.text: Some make a meal of it

explanation.surface: A sailing course, and the central part of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes main as the sea: a course of lessons on the main.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal; whimsically, also a course held at sea on the briny.

clue.text: Repeatedly going round centre of Watford

indicators.note: going round signals that the selected letters are turned backwards
the centre of the town's name gives the middle letters

explanation.surface: Circling the middle of Watford again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes TFO from Watford; 'going round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is an old poetic word for often, meaning repeatedly.

clue.text: British and French eleven given medal

parts.note: onze is French for eleven

explanation.surface: A British and French football team awarded a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven suggests a sports team, but it is the number put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze is the medal given for third place, named after its metal.

clue.text: Boss uses stratagem to stop engineers retiring

indicators.note: to stop means the trick plugs a gap, going inside the engineers
retiring means going back, so the engineers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
a ploy is a stratagem or tactic

explanation.surface: A manager uses a trick to keep engineers from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineers are the British Army's corps of Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers. 'retiring' turns their letters to EMER and 'to stop' puts the stratagem inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer is the person you work for, your boss.
